children.text: SAIS - Abu Dhabi opened its doors in 2019, launching a purposeful and transformative educational mission. From day one, the school has been deeply committed to fostering academic excellence, innovation, and global citizenship in every student.

Our journey is inspired by the visionary leadership of Her Excellency Dr. Aysha Al Sayyar and Dr. Nawaf Fawaz, who established the first SAIS campus in Sharjah in 1997, followed by campuses in Dubai (2005) and Umm Al Quwain (2012). Their forward-thinking mission was and remains clear: to nurture a generation that is academically strong, morally grounded, and future-ready.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi reception lobby

children.text: We have cultivated a culture of achievement. In just a few short years, we earned a “Very Good” rating from ADEK, with “Outstanding” recognition in key areas such as student responsibility and innovation skills. In 2024, we proudly received ADEK’s Outstanding MAP Progress Award, a testament to the dedication and excellence of our students, educators, and leadership team.

Our success is driven by a collaborative community, committed senior and middle leaders, passionate teachers, and actively engaged parents. Together, we work to fulfill our school’s mission to empower every student to reach their full potential.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi teacher guiding two students in class

children.text: Our staff communicate with stakeholders through various channels to ensure students’ wellbeing and academic success. Teachers create an inclusive environment by planning lessons that meet the needs of all learners, including students of determination and those who are gifted and talented. Student-led national and international events are regularly held at the school, helping students stay actively engaged with the wider community.

At SAIS - Abu Dhabi, we are committed to preparing our students to become lifelong learners who are curious, resilient, and driven to grow. We focus on developing strong character values such as integrity, respect, and responsibility. Through academic and personal development, we encourage our students to contribute positively to their community and make a meaningful difference in the world around them.

children.text: This journey is rooted in the visionary leadership of Her Excellency Dr. Aysha Al Sayyar and Dr. Nawaf Fawaz, who established the first SAIS campus in Sharjah in 1997, followed by the Dubai campus in 2005 and the Umm Al Quwain campus in 2012. Their forward-thinking vision was clear: to build a generation that is academically strong, morally grounded, and fully prepared for the future.

At SAIS - Abu Dhabi, we’ve cultivated a culture of achievement. In a short span of time, we have made remarkable progress, culminating in earning a “Very Good” rating from ADEK, with “Outstanding” recognition in key areas such as students’ responsibility and innovation skills. In 2024, we were honored to receive ADEK’s Outstanding MAP Progress Award, a reflection of the tireless efforts of our students, teachers, and leadership team.

heading.title: The journey of SAIS - Abu Dhabi began in 2019, marking the start of a purposeful and transformative educational mission. From its first day, the school has been deeply committed to fostering excellence, innovation, and a sense of global citizenship among its students.

children.text: Every step forward has been powered by our dedicated senior and middle leaders, our passionate teaching staff, and our engaged and supportive parent community. Together, we remain committed to realizing our school’s vision and mission, ensuring that every student is empowered to achieve their full potential.

From environmental sustainability projects to innovative STEM and Makerspace labs, from wellbeing programs to vibrant sports and extracurricular offerings, every element of our school is designed to nurture future-ready learners.
SAIS - Abu Dhabi is not just a school; it is a thriving learning community, a hub of innovation, and a place where success is not only achieved but sustained.

children.text: Dear valued students, dedicated staff, and supportive parents,

It is with great pride that I welcome you to SAIS - Abu Dhabi, a school where we nurture an enriching, inclusive environment, celebrating the uniqueness of every child and fostering a deep sense of belonging.
At SAIS, our philosophy goes beyond academics. We believe in building character and equipping students with practical life skills. Empowering future leaders who are ready to face challenges and excel in all areas of life is at the heart of our mission. This commitment to holistic development forms the foundation of our school’s vision.

We hold ourselves to the highest standards, expecting excellence from every member of our community. Guided by our mission and vision, we are committed to preparing students to become responsible, confident individuals. Throughout their educational journey, students are continuously encouraged to act as role models, demonstrating integrity, leadership, and respect in all aspects of school life.

Leadership grows through opportunity. We provide a safe, nurturing environment where students are taught to respect and value others and to engage as responsible citizens. We are proud to share that ADEK has rated us Outstanding in students’ social responsibility and innovation skills.

From Pre-KG to Grade 12, we offer a high-quality American curriculum enriched with innovation and real-world application. Our programs include STEM, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Project-Based Learning (PBL), and a strong high school program. Students benefit from a wide range of electives such as Human Anatomy, Organic Chemistry, Design & Technology, Business Studies, Programming, and AP College Board courses. As a certified SAT, AP, and IELTS center, we ensure that students are prepared for various university pathways: the General, General+, and Advanced tracks.

We also take great pride in preserving and promoting our heritage subjects, enabling students to develop a deep appreciation of local culture, Arabic language, and values.
Our dedicated teachers are committed to nurturing each student’s growth academically, socially, and emotionally. We strive not only to help students meet high standards but to exceed their own expectations. Parents are key partners in this journey, and we deeply value their involvement and voice through committees like the Parent Advisory Council and National Identity Committee.

Beyond the classroom, we offer a rich After-School Activities (ASA) program and a variety of extracurricular opportunities, including MUN (Model United Nations), public speaking, arts conferences, and more. Our students actively contribute to the Abu Dhabi community by completing internal and external volunteer service hours, strengthening their leadership skills and engagement.
We believe in education that makes a tangible, positive difference in the lives of our students and equips them with the skills they need for lifelong sustainable success.
It would be an honor to welcome you to our SAIS community. Together, let us continue building a future rooted in excellence, compassion, and ambition.

Sincerely,
Ms. Ban Al Duri
Principal

children.text: The Abu Dhabi Department of Education and Knowledge (ADEK) is the regulatory authority responsible for overseeing and enhancing the quality of education across schools in Abu Dhabi. Through its comprehensive inspection framework, ADEK evaluates schools against key standards including student achievement, teaching and assessment, curriculum quality, student wellbeing, and leadership. We are proud to share that our school has been awarded a “Very Good” rating in the 2024–2025 ADEK Irtiqa’a inspection, reflecting our strong commitment to academic excellence, high-quality teaching and learning, student care, and continuous school improvement.

children.text: Elementary students engage in a comprehensive curriculum driven by project-based learning (PBL) and the scientific method in math, English, and science. They benefit from weekly sessions in swimming, physical education (PE), and gymnastics to support their physical development. The curriculum is enriched with music, art, drama, and French, in addition to Arabic plays and Qur’an recitation to strengthen cultural identity and creativity. Students are introduced to AI and STEM foundations, developing 21st-century skills at an early age.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi elementary teacher guiding students through a hands-on building activity

children.text: In Grades 1 and 2, SAIS - Abu Dhabi is implementing an ongoing assessment model designed to provide a comprehensive and holistic view of each student’s progress. This shift moves away from solely relying on periodic tests and instead focuses on continuous evaluation through observations, classwork, homework, projects, discussions, and quizzes. This approach enables teachers to better understand and support students’ development throughout the year in a relaxed and stress-free environment.

children.text: While multiple formative and summative assessments will take place across subjects, parents will not be informed prior to their administration to ensure assessments reflect authentic learning and reduce performance anxiety. However, in response to parent feedback and to support home preparation, schedules will be shared in advance for Arabic and Islamic Studies assessments only.

We continue using our proficiency scale for Grades 1 and 2 to better reflect the progress and achievements of our students. We do convert these proficiency scales into percentages for our internal data analyses.

children.text: Arabic Language Curriculum
Motto:
“I Read with Understanding… Write with Creativity… and Express Myself with Confidence.”
For Arab Students:

The curriculum focuses on developing fluent reading, accurate writing, and confident self-expression. It encourages students to communicate their ideas effectively while strengthening independent learning, comprehension, and critical thinking skills.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum follows a progressive approach to developing reading, writing, and speaking skills. It emphasizes building essential vocabulary and a solid foundation in Arabic grammar, enabling students to communicate effectively and confidently in various everyday situations.
Islamic Education Curriculum
For Arab Students:

The curriculum focuses on strengthening students’ understanding of the Holy Quran, the Sunnah of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), Islamic beliefs, and acts of worship. It connects Islamic teachings with moral values and authentic Emirati customs and traditions, encouraging students to apply these principles in their daily lives.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum introduces fundamental Islamic concepts through accessible and engaging learning experiences. It emphasizes moral values, tolerance, and the memorization of short Quranic surahs, using simplified language and age-appropriate teaching methods to ensure understanding and meaningful participation in the learning process.
Social Studies Curriculum
For Arab and Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum aims to foster a strong sense of pride in the UAE’s rich cultural heritage while promoting the values of citizenship, tolerance, and national identity. Through observation and inquiry, Arab and non-Arab students gain a comprehensive understanding of the UAE’s history and culture.

Daily schedules also include lab-based science, design and technology, computer-based learning, and volunteering opportunities, all aligned with graduation requirements and personal development.

children.text: High School Pathways function like college majors, but begin during the high school experience. Every student can benefit from selecting and following a sequence of career-related classes aligned with their interests.
A Pathway:
Provides a sequence of courses within your area of interest
Connects your career interests from high school to college and/or career
Serves as an educational roadmap guiding you to relevant high school courses and postsecondary options
Helps you acquire knowledge and skills linked to specific postsecondary programs leading to certificates, degrees, and careers

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi high school student painting a model in art class

cards.description:
Students in this pathway solve problems, develop new technologies, and drive innovation. This rigorous college preparatory curriculum focuses on advanced mathematics and science, preparing students for university-level work.

Participants apply essential math and science content in real-world contexts. Career possibilities range from science and math educators to laboratory technicians to NASA astronauts.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi high school students walking with their teacher in the girls section

cards.title: Science and Engineering Pathway

cards.description:
Students gain hands-on foundational skills in their chosen mode of expression, including:

•	Studio art
•	Fashion design
•	Interior design
•	Acting
•	Theater production
•	Vocal and instrumental performance
•	Film and audio production

This pathway develops cultural awareness alongside communication, creative, and critical thinking skills necessary for success across various fields. Graduates may seek direct employment as artists, musicians, designers, actors, or audio producers, or pursue bachelor’s or graduate degrees for careers in teaching, art direction, theater production, fashion, interior design, media arts, and film.

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi teacher guiding two high school students sketching in art class

cards.title: Visual and Performing Arts Pathway

cards.description:
This pathway provides students with opportunities to develop skills for customer-focused careers and gain experience in technology, communication, and management. Students explore business ownership fundamentals and practice developing business plans while learning to organize and direct business operations.

Students investigate financial management, including how industry standards, economic factors, technological advancements, international influences, social trends, legal requirements, and ethical considerations impact business decisions. They learn to formulate and interpret financial information for decision-making, compliance, and risk management.

Career opportunities include entrepreneurship, sales, marketing, economics, management, accounting, banking, securities and investments, and other financial specializations.

children.text: Advanced Placement (AP) is a College Board program that allows high school students to take courses that can earn college credits and/or qualify them for advanced university classes. AP courses are weighted (1.25), provided students achieve qualifying scores on the respective College Board exams.
AP classes are optional. All enrolled students must sit for the College Board AP exam and cover the cost of required resources and exams.

children.text: Arabic Language Curriculum
Motto:
“A Language That Shapes Identity… Minds That Shape the Future.”
For Arab Students:

The curriculum aims to develop a generation of confident leaders equipped with advanced skills in critical text analysis, creative expression, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence and modern technology. Through approved curricula and enriching digital learning platforms, students strengthen their analytical, linguistic, and communication skills, preparing them for higher education and future academic success.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum empowers students to use Arabic for essential academic and professional communication while developing a deeper understanding of the cultural values and traditions of their surrounding environment. It equips students with practical language skills that broaden their career opportunities and encourage meaningful participation in the community.
Islamic Education Curriculum
For Arab Students:

The curriculum focuses on developing well-rounded, responsible individuals who take pride in their Islamic and national identities. Students are encouraged to draw inspiration from distinguished national role models, particularly the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan (may Allah have mercy on him), whose leadership, values, and legacy continue to inspire future generations.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum promotes a balanced and moderate understanding of Islamic principles while fostering global citizenship, tolerance, and mutual respect. It strengthens students’ critical thinking skills, enabling them to approach contemporary issues thoughtfully and responsibly while embracing the values of peaceful coexistence and cultural understanding.
Social Studies Curriculum
For Arab and Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum equips students with scientific research, source evaluation, and decision-making skills, enabling them to discuss local and global issues and propose innovative solutions that contribute to sustainable development and shape the future.

children.text: Arabic Language Curriculum
Motto:
“We Analyze Deeply… Think Critically… and Create Through Language.”
For Arab Students:

The curriculum focuses on analyzing and critically evaluating literary and informational texts, supporting arguments with relevant evidence, and developing higher-order thinking skills. Students are encouraged to integrate modern technologies into their learning experiences, enhancing their ability to construct knowledge, think independently, and express ideas creatively.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum advances students’ language proficiency by strengthening reading comprehension, developing more extensive writing skills, and encouraging meaningful, in-depth conversations. It also promotes an understanding of the cultural dimensions of the Arabic language through carefully selected texts appropriate to students’ academic and linguistic levels.
Islamic Education Curriculum
For Arab Students:

The curriculum deepens students’ understanding of Islamic principles, Quranic interpretation (Tafsir), Hadith, and Islamic teachings. It encourages students to draw inspiration from the exemplary character of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), influential Islamic figures, and national role models, fostering strong moral values and responsible behavior.
For Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum introduces students to the life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and fundamental Islamic moral values through approaches tailored to their linguistic and cultural backgrounds. It promotes a deeper understanding of the role of Islam in shaping society and encourages students to apply ethical principles in their daily lives.
Social Studies Curriculum
For Arab and Non-Arab Students:

The curriculum shapes students’ awareness of the UAE’s history, geography, and achievements, and develops their ability to analyze social and environmental issues and practice positive citizenship, while providing language and cultural support for non-Arab students.

cards.description:
The Cognitive Abilities Test (CAT4) helps us understand how students learn and their academic potential. Students in Grades 3–9 take this assessment upon enrollment to identify their learning styles, enabling teachers to:

•	Adapt teaching approaches and materials
•	Adjust instructional pace and emphasis
•	Implement differentiated instruction

CAT4 measures four types of reasoning:

•	Verbal Reasoning - Understanding and reasoning through words
•	Quantitative Reasoning - Using numerical skills for problem-solving
•	Non-verbal Reasoning - Problem-solving using visual information
•	Spatial Ability - Thinking and drawing conclusions in three dimensions

image.alt: SAIS - Abu Dhabi students working on a written task in class

cards.title: CAT4 Assessment

•	Phonics knowledge

•	Decoding ability
•	Vocabulary development
•	Grammatical understanding
•	Deduction and inference skills
•	Understanding of figurative and idiomatic language

The Arabic Subjects Department at our school is committed to nurturing generations of students who are linguistically proficient, deeply connected to their national and Islamic identities, and creative thinkers prepared to lead the future. Through a comprehensive and integrated curriculum, we combine the authenticity of our values and traditions with the latest educational technologies and innovative teaching approaches.
Arabic Language

In Arabic Language Education, we begin by fostering curiosity, exploration, and learning through play in Kindergarten. As students progress through Elementary, Middle, and High School, they develop from foundational language fluency and creative expression to advanced critical thinking, textual analysis, and the responsible use of artificial intelligence and technology. Our approach is supported by approved curricula and enriching digital learning platforms that enhance students’ linguistic abilities, creativity, and communication skills.
Islamic Education

In Islamic Education, we strive to instill a deep appreciation for Islamic values and teachings, encouraging students to develop a love for their faith, memorize the Holy Quran, and learn from the noble life and teachings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). We also inspire students to follow the example of influential national figures, particularly the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan (may Allah have mercy on him), whose values and legacy continue to shape the UAE. Interactive activities and engaging learning experiences further strengthen students’ understanding and application of Islamic principles in their daily lives.
Social Studies

In Social Studies, we aim to develop responsible global citizens who take pride in the UAE’s rich cultural heritage and values of tolerance while acquiring essential research, inquiry, and future-thinking skills. Our progressive curriculum embraces linguistic differences and cultural diversity, ensuring an inclusive and enriching learning experience for both Arab and non-Arab students.

Through these three interconnected disciplines, we are dedicated to delivering high-quality education that aligns with the vision and aspirations of the United Arab Emirates, preparing tomorrow’s leaders with the knowledge, strong moral values, creativity, and innovative thinking needed to succeed in an ever-changing world.

children.text: The application process begins with the parent/guardian completing the official application form and signing the Entry Requirements and Commitment documents.
Once submitted to the Registrar’s Office, our team will schedule a specific date for your child’s placement assessments and interview.

Prospective students seeking admission will take placement tests in English and Mathematics as the first step in the admissions process. Test results will be reviewed by the relevant Head of School, Student Support Department, Deputy Principal, or the school Principal.
Parents or guardians will be contacted to arrange an interview for you and your child/children.
Following successful completion of all placement requirements, the registration process commences. During this stage, parents/guardians must submit all required documentation to finalize enrollment.
For comprehensive information regarding registration procedures, the fee structure, curriculum details, and additional school information, please consult the 2025 School Guide.
When applying, please provide the following documents:
Original Emirates ID cards (parents and child)
Previous school academic records
Parents’ passport copies with visa pages
Child’s vaccination records
Child’s birth certificate
Eight passport-sized photographs
